title: MeanFlow for Molecular Conformation Generation: One-Step 3D Structure Prediction via Average Velocity Fields
description:
Problem: Generating accurate 3D molecular conformations is critical for drug discovery, but current diffusion/flow-based methods require hundreds of function evaluations, making virtual screening of large chemical libraries prohibitively expensive. One-step generation methods have not been systematically explored for structured 3D graph outputs like molecules.

Proposed Method: We adapt the MeanFlow framework to SE(3)-equivariant generation of molecular conformations. We define average velocity fields over atomic coordinates and torsion angles in SE(3)-invariant space, deriving the mean-flow identity for equivariant networks (E(n)-GNNs). The model jointly predicts inter-atomic distances and dihedral angles in a single forward pass without distillation or pre-training. We introduce a geometry-aware average velocity parameterization that respects bond length and angle constraints via projected flows on the molecular configuration manifold.

Experiments: (1) Benchmark on GEOM-DRUGS and GEOM-QM9 datasets measuring coverage/AMR metrics vs. multi-step baselines (Torsional Diffusion, GeoDiff, FlowMol). (2) Ablation comparing instantaneous vs. average velocity parameterizations for equivariant networks. (3) Wall-clock speedup analysis for virtual screening scenarios. (4) Downstream docking accuracy (Vina scores) to validate generated conformations for drug-like molecules. We expect 50-100x speedup with competitive geometric accuracy.

Problem: Generating accurate 3D molecular conformations is critical for drug discovery, but current diffusion/flow-based approaches (e.g., Torsional Diffusion, EquiFold) require hundreds of NFEs, creating a bottleneck for high-throughput virtual screening of millions of compounds.

Proposed Method: We adapt the MeanFlow framework to SE(3)-equivariant molecular conformation generation. Rather than modeling instantaneous velocities over torsion angles or Cartesian coordinates, we parameterize average velocities using an equivariant graph neural network (E(3)-GNN) backbone. We derive the average-to-instantaneous velocity identity in the context of SE(3) manifolds and torsional space, handling periodicity constraints. The model maps a random noise conformation directly to a chemically valid 3D structure in a single forward pass, trained from scratch without distillation from a teacher model.

Experiments: (1) Benchmark on GEOM-DRUGS and GEOM-QM9 datasets measuring coverage and AMR metrics vs. multi-step baselines; (2) Compare 1-NFE MeanFlow against distilled single-step variants of Torsional Diffusion; (3) Evaluate wall-clock throughput for virtual screening scenarios (10^6 molecule sampling); (4) Ablate the average velocity identity term versus standard flow matching on conformational diversity. We hypothesize 10-50x speedup with <5% quality degradation versus multi-step methods.

title: MeanFlow for Discrete Tokens: One-Step Generative Modeling in Latent Codebook Spaces
description: Problem: One-step generative models like MeanFlow operate in continuous spaces, but modern multimodal systems (LLM-based image generation, audio synthesis, protein design) increasingly rely on discrete tokenized representations. Adapting flow-based one-step generation to discrete codebook latent spaces remains unsolved, as standard ODE trajectories are ill-defined over discrete domains. Proposed Method: We reformulate average velocity in the context of soft-relaxed discrete spaces. During training, we embed codebook tokens into a continuous simplex via temperature-annealed Gumbel-softmax relaxation, define MeanFlow's average velocity identity over these continuous embeddings, and project back to discrete tokens at inference. We introduce a codebook-aware loss that penalizes trajectories landing off-manifold (far from valid embeddings), replacing the standard flow matching regression with a hybrid objective combining MeanFlow's self-consistency identity and a nearest-neighbor codebook alignment term. Experiments: (1) Class-conditional ImageNet generation using a VQ-VAE tokenizer, comparing 1-NFE FID against discrete diffusion baselines (MAGE, MaskGIT) and continuous MeanFlow; (2) Text-to-audio generation on AudioCaps; (3) Protein sequence design on CATH benchmarks. Ablations study the effect of Gumbel temperature scheduling and codebook alignment weight on generation quality and codebook utilization.

title: MeanFlow for Conditional Scientific Field Generation: One-Step Emulation of Physics Simulations
description: Problem: High-fidelity physics simulations (climate models, fluid dynamics, cosmological N-body) are computationally prohibitive, and existing neural emulators either sacrifice accuracy or require many inference steps, limiting real-time applications. Method: We adapt the MeanFlow framework to conditional scientific field generation, where the model learns average velocity fields conditioned on physical parameters (e.g., initial conditions, boundary conditions, forcing terms). We introduce a physics-informed MeanFlow objective that augments the average-instantaneous velocity identity with PDE residual penalties, ensuring generated fields respect known governing equations. To handle the structured, high-dimensional nature of scientific fields (3D volumetric data with physical symmetries), we incorporate equivariant architectures within the MeanFlow backbone and train with multi-scale loss functions sensitive to spectral properties critical in physics (energy spectra, structure functions). Experiments: (1) 2D/3D turbulent fluid flow emulation vs. Navier-Stokes solver ground truth, measuring spectral fidelity and divergence-free constraint satisfaction; (2) climate downscaling on ERA5 data conditioned on coarse-resolution inputs; (3) cosmological density field generation conditioned on cosmological parameters. We compare against multi-step diffusion emulators, GANs, and standard Flow Matching, demonstrating that MeanFlow achieves competitive accuracy with 10-50x inference speedup, enabling ensemble uncertainty quantification at scale.

title: MeanFlow for Consistent Video Generation: Extending Average Velocity Frameworks to Temporal Coherence
description:
Problem: One-step generative models like MeanFlow achieve remarkable image quality but extending them to video generation remains largely unexplored. Video synthesis requires not only high per-frame quality but temporal coherence across frames, which poses unique challenges for one-step methods that must simultaneously capture spatial and temporal dynamics in a single forward pass.

Proposed Method: We extend the MeanFlow average velocity framework to video generation by introducing a spatiotemporal average velocity field that operates over both spatial dimensions and the temporal axis. We derive a generalized identity relating spatiotemporal average and instantaneous velocities, and introduce a temporal consistency regularization term that penalizes optical-flow discrepancies between adjacent generated frames. The model is trained from scratch without distillation using a 3D U-ViT architecture, with the average velocity parameterization applied across the joint space-time transport path.

Experiments: We evaluate on UCF-101 and Kinetics-600 benchmarks measuring FVD and IS scores at 1-NFE. We compare against multi-step video diffusion models (VideoLDM, CogVideo) and one-step baselines (consistency models adapted for video). Ablations isolate contributions of temporal consistency regularization vs. spatiotemporal average velocity. We also analyze inference speed vs. quality tradeoffs and conduct human preference studies on temporal smoothness, demonstrating practical viability for real-time video synthesis applications.

title: MeanFlow for Conditional Video Generation: Extending Average Velocity Fields to Spatiotemporal Domains
description:

The challenge is extending the average velocity framework to handle the spatiotemporal correlations and higher-dimensional manifolds inherent in video data.

Specifically, we parameterize the average velocity network as a 3D-attention transformer that processes flattened space-time tokens, and derive a spatiotemporal identity between average and instantaneous velocities that accounts for temporal causal structure. We additionally introduce a temporal coherence regularizer that penalizes inconsistent average velocity estimates across overlapping time windows, encouraging smooth motion trajectories without requiring multi-step sampling.

Experiments: (1) Train single-step video generation models on UCF-101 and Kinetics-600 at 256x256 resolution, 16 frames; (2) Compare FVD and IS against multi-step baselines (VideoLDM, CogVideo) and one-step distillation methods; (3) Ablate the temporal coherence regularizer and 3D vs. factorized attention; (4) Evaluate inference throughput for real-time applications (frames per second). title: MeanFlow for Inverse Problems: Average Velocity Guidance for One-Step Medical Image Reconstruction
description: Problem: Solving inverse problems (MRI/CT reconstruction, deblurring, super-resolution) with diffusion/flow models typically requires hundreds of function evaluations, making clinical deployment impractical. Existing one-step distillation approaches for inverse problems rely on multi-step teacher models and complex training pipelines, limiting their accessibility. Proposed Method: We extend MeanFlow's average velocity framework to conditional inverse problem solving by deriving a measurement-consistent average velocity identity. Specifically, we incorporate likelihood guidance directly into the MeanFlow objective using a tractable approximation of the posterior mean velocity: v̄_θ(x_t, t_0, t_1) conditioned on degraded measurements y. We propose a Measurement-Consistent MeanFlow (MC-MeanFlow) loss that combines the original average/instantaneous velocity identity with a data-consistency penalty computed in measurement space, requiring no pre-trained unconditional teacher. The model is trained end-to-end from scratch on paired (clean, degraded) data. Planned Experiments: (1) MRI acceleration (4x, 8x undersampling) on fastMRI knee/brain datasets; (2) CT sparse-view reconstruction on AAPM dataset; (3) natural image super-resolution (4x, 8x) on ImageNet. We compare against DPS, DDRM, DDNM (multi-step), and consistency model baselines on PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS metrics, demonstrating competitive reconstruction quality at 1-NFE with wall-clock speedups exceeding 100x over multi-step competitors.

title: MeanFlow for Discrete Tokens: One-Step Generative Modeling in Latent Codebook Spaces
description: Problem: One-step generative models like MeanFlow operate in continuous latent spaces, but state-of-the-art image and video generation increasingly relies on discrete tokenizers (VQ-VAE, VQGAN, FSQ). Bridging MeanFlow's average-velocity framework to discrete codebook spaces would enable ultra-fast generation in the dominant discrete paradigm without multi-step sampling or distillation. Proposed Method: We reformulate average velocity over continuous interpolation paths in the embedding space of discrete codebooks, defining a 'soft trajectory' between noise embeddings and quantized target embeddings. We introduce a straight-path interpolation in embedding space that respects codebook geometry, then apply the MeanFlow identity to train a network predicting average velocity end-to-end. At inference, a single forward pass produces a continuous embedding that is nearest-neighbor quantized to a codebook token sequence, decoded by the existing tokenizer. We also explore a learned temperature annealing at quantization to reduce discretization error. Experiments: (1) Class-conditional ImageNet 256×256 generation with VQGAN and FSQ tokenizers, comparing FID/IS at 1-NFE against AR baselines (LlamaGen, RQ-Transformer) and masked diffusion models (MaskGIT). (2) Ablations on codebook size and embedding-space interpolation strategies. (3) Extension to text-to-image with a CLIP-conditioned variant to test generalization.

title: MeanFlow for Inverse Problems: One-Step Posterior Sampling via Average Velocity Guidance
description: Problem: Diffusion/flow-based solvers for inverse problems (e.g., MRI reconstruction, image inpainting, super-resolution) typically require hundreds of neural function evaluations (NFEs) during inference, making them impractical for clinical or real-time settings. This allows the network to learn average velocities that simultaneously satisfy the transport identity and remain faithful to the forward measurement model, without requiring multi-step unrolling at inference. We further propose a self-supervised training variant using only degraded measurements, avoiding the need for paired ground-truth data. Experiments: We evaluate on (1) Gaussian deblurring, (2) accelerated MRI (4x, 8x), (3) inpainting, and (4) super-resolution (4x) on standard benchmarks (FFHQ, ImageNet, fastMRI). We compare against DPS, DDRM, ΠGDM, and flow-matching distillation baselines across PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, and NFE metrics, demonstrating competitive reconstruction quality at 1-NFE.

title: MeanFlow for Conditional Video Generation: Average Velocity Fields in Spatiotemporal Domains
description:

Experiments: We train on UCF-101 and WebVid-10M benchmarks, evaluating FVD and CLIP-similarity scores against multi-step baselines (VideoCrafter, ModelScope) and one-step distillation methods (AnimateLCM, FlowDistillation). title: MeanFlow for Conditional Generation with Classifier-Free Guidance: Distillation-Free One-Step Text-to-Image Synthesis
description: Problem: While MeanFlow achieves impressive one-step generation on class-conditional ImageNet, extending the average velocity framework to text-to-image synthesis with classifier-free guidance (CFG) remains unexplored. Proposed Method: We reformulate MeanFlow to natively incorporate CFG by defining average velocity over guidance-augmented flows. Specifically, we derive a modified identity relating average and instantaneous velocities under the combined conditional/unconditional flow field, parameterized by guidance scale w. We train a single network that accepts w as an explicit conditioning input, allowing it to learn average velocities across the guidance spectrum simultaneously. This enables one-step generation at arbitrary guidance scales without separate distillation. We also investigate a guidance-adaptive timestep weighting scheme to improve training stability across the w range. Experiments: We train on CC12M and LAION-Aesthetics, evaluating FID, CLIP score, and human preference metrics against Flow Matching baselines, consistency distillation, and ADD. We ablate guidance scale conditioning, the modified velocity identity, and compare 1-NFE vs 2-NFE performance to establish scaling behavior of our approach.

title: MeanFlow for Controllable Video Generation: Extending Average Velocity Fields to Temporal Consistency in One-Step Text-to-Video Synthesis
description: Problem: One-step generative modeling has achieved impressive results for images, but video generation remains dominated by expensive multi-step diffusion processes requiring 20-50 NFEs, making real-time or interactive video synthesis impractical. title: MeanFlow for Discrete Tokens: One-Step Generative Modeling in Latent Codebook Spaces
description: Problem: MeanFlow demonstrates impressive continuous image generation, but many modern generative systems operate over discrete token spaces (e.g., LLM-style image/video/audio tokenizers, VQ-VAE codebooks). Adapting flow-based one-step generation to discrete domains is non-trivial since flow matching relies on continuous interpolation paths. Proposal: We extend the MeanFlow average-velocity framework to operate in the continuous embedding space of learned discrete codebooks, introducing a 'soft quantization bridge' that defines interpolation paths between noise and quantized latent codes. Specifically, we model flows between Gaussian noise and soft codebook embeddings, applying MeanFlow's average velocity identity to train a one-step generator that maps directly to the nearest codebook entry at inference. We further propose a codebook-aware loss that penalizes average velocity fields pointing toward off-manifold regions between codebook entries, encouraging the model to learn straighter trajectories toward valid discrete tokens. Experiments: (1) Class-conditional image generation using VQGAN tokenizers on ImageNet 256x256, measuring FID and IS at 1-NFE; (2) Text-to-image generation with discrete token representations; (3) Ablation of soft quantization temperature and codebook-aware regularization strength; (4) Comparison against discrete diffusion models and multi-step VQ-based flow models, demonstrating comparable quality with dramatically reduced sampling cost.

title: MeanFlow for Conditional Scientific Field Generation: One-Step Surrogate Modeling for Turbulent Flow Simulations
description: Problem: High-fidelity computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations of turbulent flows require enormous compute, creating a bottleneck for design optimization and uncertainty quantification. Existing neural surrogates either sacrifice accuracy or require iterative sampling (diffusion-based) that remains slow at inference time. The model is trained from scratch on datasets of 2D/3D Navier-Stokes simulation snapshots. Experiments: We evaluate on the FNO benchmark datasets (Navier-Stokes, airfoil pressure fields) and a new 3D turbulence dataset, measuring: velocity/pressure field RMSE, turbulent kinetic energy spectra error, divergence residuals, and wall-clock speedup versus CFD. We compare against Flow Matching surrogates, diffusion-based surrogates, and FNO baselines, demonstrating that MeanFlow achieves competitive accuracy with 100-1000x speedup at inference.

title: MeanFlow for Discrete Tokens: One-Step Generative Modeling in Language and Code
description:
Problem: One-step generative modeling has transformed image synthesis, but language and code generation still rely on autoregressive or multi-step diffusion models with high inference cost. The average velocity identity from MeanFlow guides training without distillation. We additionally propose a token-consistency regularization loss that encourages the one-step prediction to produce coherent token sequences by penalizing perplexity under a frozen language model. The model is trained end-to-end from scratch on text/code corpora.

Experiments: (1) Unconditional text generation on LM1B and WikiText-103, measuring perplexity and MAUVE against autoregressive baselines and discrete diffusion models. (2) Code generation on HumanEval/MBPP benchmarks, measuring pass@k and wall-clock inference speedup. (3) Ablations on embedding dimensionality, quantization strategies, and the token-consistency regularization weight. We target competitive perplexity with 10-50x fewer function evaluations than diffusion-based text models.

title: MeanFlow for Molecular Conformer Generation: One-Step 3D Structure Prediction via Average Velocity Fields

title: MeanFlow for Conditional Scientific Field Generation: One-Step Climate and Fluid Dynamics Emulation

Experiments: (1) 2D Navier-Stokes super-resolution, comparing FID, RMSE, and divergence error against consistency models and rectified flow distillation; (2) ERA5 climate downscaling (coarse-to-fine precipitation fields); (3) ensemble spread calibration vs. multi-step DDPM baselines. title: MeanFlow for Conditional Scientific Field Generation: One-Step Surrogate Modeling for Turbulent Flow Simulation

title: MeanFlow for Conditional Video Generation: Extending Average Velocity Fields to Spatiotemporal Synthesis
description:

title: MeanFlow for Inverse Problems: One-Step Posterior Sampling via Average Velocity Guidance
description:
Problem: Diffusion/flow-based solvers for inverse problems (deblurring, super-resolution, compressed sensing, MRI reconstruction) typically require dozens to hundreds of NFEs at inference, making them impractical in clinical or real-time settings. Specifically, we decompose the average velocity field into an unconditional MeanFlow prior term plus a likelihood-gradient correction computed via the identity relating average and instantaneous velocities. This allows plug-and-play guidance: a single pretrained unconditional MeanFlow model is combined at inference with a differentiable forward operator, requiring only one network evaluation plus one gradient step. We also propose a fine-tuning variant where the average velocity is conditioned on degraded measurements via cross-attention, trained with paired data using the MeanFlow self-consistency loss augmented with a data-fidelity term.

Experiments: (1) Natural image restoration benchmarks (FFHQ, ImageNet): inpainting, deblurring, 4×/8× super-resolution. (2) Accelerated MRI reconstruction (fastMRI, 4×/8× undersampling). title: MeanFlow for Controllable Video Generation: Extending Average Velocity Fields to Temporal Dynamics
description:

We derive a spatiotemporal identity analogous to the MeanFlow identity, relating average velocities across the full video volume to instantaneous velocities, and use this to train a 3D U-ViT network from scratch without distillation. We introduce a temporal consistency regularization term that penalizes average velocity inconsistencies between overlapping temporal windows, encouraging smooth motion in single-step generated videos.

Experiments: We evaluate on UCF-101 and Kinetics-600 benchmarks measuring FVD and IS at 1-NFE. We compare against consistency distillation baselines, ADD-adapted video models, and multi-step video diffusion models. Ablations examine temporal window sizes, the spatiotemporal identity weighting, and scaling behavior from 4-frame to 16-frame clips, targeting competitive FVD at dramatically reduced inference cost.

title: MeanFlow for Conditional Scientific Field Generation: One-Step Surrogate Modeling for Turbulence and Climate Simulations
description:
Problem: Physics simulations (turbulence, climate, fluid dynamics) require expensive iterative solvers. Diffusion/flow-based surrogates show promise but multi-step inference remains too slow for real-time or ensemble applications. Existing one-step distillation methods degrade physical fidelity (energy spectra, divergence-free constraints).

Proposed Method: We adapt MeanFlow's average velocity framework to conditional scientific field generation, incorporating physics-informed constraints directly into the mean flow identity. Specifically, we augment the MeanFlow training objective with: (1) a spectral consistency loss penalizing deviations in turbulent kinetic energy spectra, (2) a soft divergence-free penalty for incompressible flows embedded in the average-velocity regression target, and (3) conditioning on coarse-grid states or boundary conditions via cross-attention. The self-contained training (no distillation) makes this practical since no expensive teacher multi-step rollouts are needed.

Experiments: (a) 2D Navier-Stokes turbulence generation conditioned on Reynolds number — evaluate FID, energy spectrum error, enstrophy; (b) ERA5 climate field downscaling (coarse→fine resolution) — RMSE, power spectra, extreme event statistics; (c) Wall-clock speedup vs. numerical solvers and multi-step flow baselines. We expect 100-1000x speedup over solvers while preserving physical statistics better than prior one-step approaches.

title: MeanFlow for Molecular Conformation Generation: One-Step 3D Structure Prediction via Average Velocity Fields
description: Problem: Generating valid 3D molecular conformations is critical for drug discovery, but current diffusion/flow-based methods (e.g., Torsional Diffusion, EquiFM) require hundreds of NFEs, creating bottlenecks in virtual screening pipelines where millions of molecules must be evaluated. One-step generation methods have not been explored for this structured, SE(3)-equivariant domain. Proposed Method: We extend MeanFlow's average velocity framework to SE(3)-equivariant neural networks for molecular conformation generation. We define average velocity fields over torsion angle space and Cartesian coordinates jointly, deriving the MeanFlow identity adapted for equivariant architectures (e.g., EGNN or EquiformerV2 backbone). The average velocity network takes as input a molecular graph, current coordinates, and interval endpoints (t,s), predicting the mean displacement that maps noise to valid 3D conformers in a single step. We incorporate chirality and ring planarity constraints through auxiliary loss terms. Experiments: We evaluate on GEOM-QM9 and GEOM-DRUGS benchmarks, measuring coverage and AMR metrics against DFT-optimized reference conformers. We compare against Torsional Diffusion, GeoDiff, and EquiFM at matched NFEs. We additionally benchmark on a virtual screening task (docking score correlation) to demonstrate practical speedups, targeting >50x inference acceleration with competitive coverage scores.

title: MeanFlow for Molecule Generation: Average Velocity Fields for One-Step 3D Conformer Synthesis
description:
Problem: Generating valid 3D molecular conformers currently requires expensive multi-step diffusion or flow-matching processes over SE(3)-equivariant spaces, creating a bottleneck for high-throughput drug discovery screening. One-step generation for molecules remains largely unexplored due to the geometric complexity of atomic coordinate and bond geometry distributions.

Proposed Method: We extend the MeanFlow framework to SE(3)-equivariant architectures by defining average velocity fields over equivariant features (atomic positions, orientations) using E(n)-equivariant graph neural networks. We derive the average-instantaneous velocity identity for Riemannian manifolds (specifically SE(3)) and use it as a self-supervised training signal without distillation. We introduce a geometry-aware interpolation scheme between noise and target conformers that respects molecular symmetries, enabling the average velocity parameterization to remain equivariant throughout training.

Experiments: (1) Conformer generation quality on GEOM-DRUGS and QM9 benchmarks, measuring coverage/matching metrics vs. RDKit, EDM, and multi-step flow models; (2) One-step vs. multi-step NFE tradeoff curves showing quality vs. compute; (3) Validity/uniqueness/novelty metrics for de novo 3D molecular generation; (4) Downstream docking score evaluation for generated molecules; (5) Ablations on the equivariant average velocity identity and interpolation schemes. Success is demonstrated by matching multi-step baselines with 1-NFE.
